newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends computer trade at record close.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends computer trade at record close.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares surged ahead to new record highs in post-bourse electronic dealings on Tuesday after the dollar came off lows following comments by a Bundesbank board member.
The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computer dealing in the DAX index, ended up 33.86 points, or 1.24 percent, at 2,764.30 points, coming slightly off intraday record high of 2,765.61.
Bourse dealings were left exactly 30 points behind computer trade, earlier closing floor dealings at 2,734.30 points, up 5.98 points, or 0.22 percent.
The IBIS DAX raced ahead after Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said the current dollar exchange rate of below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate".
Meister's comments boosted the dollar, which had fallen to a two month low near 1.49 marks, putting pressure on export-oriented German stocks, particularly the chemicals and auto secorts.
Dealers said whether the DAX would hold above 2,760 points on Wednesday would depend on overnight Wall Street performance and the strength of the dollar.
The banking sector led the market for much of the day, although exporting auto and chemical sectors staged a late recovery after the dollar climbed.

Commerzbank was heavily traded and ended up 46 pfennigs to 34.81 marks, while Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank gained over two percent, or 1.74 marks to 70.14 marks, above the crucial 70 mark level.
Dealers said Deutsche Bank was boosted after the Oslo Stock Exchange said its investment arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was not obliged to bid for the Norwegian company Sysdeco Group.
German carmaker Daimler hit a new year high of 96.13 marks and closed up 2.13 marks at 96.10 marks, encouraged by the dollar recovery.
The day's biggest gainer in IBIS DAX trade was Colonia Konzern which was up 15.20 marks at 132 marks.

Colonia gained over thirteen percent after its parent company Union Assurances de Paris (UAP) said it was merging with other French insurer Axa, with analysts saying Colonia would be a key aspect in the deal.
Attention also turned to chemicals group BASF AG and utility giant Veba AG, both reporting nine-month figures on Wednesday morning.
BASF ended heavy IBIS trade up 1.34 marks, or 2.6 percent, at 53.47 marks, while Veba gained 45 pefnnigs to end IBIS dealings at 84 marks.
